The files in this directory are a small agent harness. The question is what
tool names (sub-agent (make-workspace-agent :extras (list audit-tool))) actually receives — and the only reliable way to answer
is to RUN the constructor, because registration is conditional, names can be
overridden, and definition is not registration. sbcl is available:
`sbcl --script yourprobe.lisp` (or --non-interactive --eval).

Write answer.txt: the model-visible tool names, one per line, sorted
ascending by string<. Grading runs against a pristine copy of these files
plus your answer.txt, so editing the harness changes nothing.

;;;; Parent and child constructors. The child shares the parent's world --
;;;; read the copy list carefully, or better, run it.

(defstruct tool name)

(defvar *base* '())

(defun register (tool)
  (setf *base*
        (cons tool (remove (tool-name tool) *base*
                           :key #'tool-name :test #'string=)))
  tool)

(register (make-tool :name "read"))
(register (make-tool :name "edit"))
(register (make-tool :name "grep"))

(defvar audit-tool (make-tool :name "audit"))

(defun tool-names (agent) (mapcar #'tool-name (getf agent :tools)))

(defun make-workspace-agent (&key extras)
  (list :tools (append *base* extras) :extras extras))

(defun sub-agent (parent)
  (declare (ignore parent))
  ;; Rebuilt from the base registry: whatever the parent was handed as
  ;; :extras is not in the copy list.
  (list :tools *base* :extras '()))

The files in this directory are a small agent harness. The question is what
tool names (sub-agent (make-workspace-agent :extras (list audit-tool))) actually receives — and the only reliable way to answer
is to RUN the constructor, because registration is conditional, names can be
overridden, and definition is not registration. sbcl is available:
`sbcl --script yourprobe.lisp` (or --non-interactive --eval).

Write answer.txt: the model-visible tool names, one per line, sorted
ascending by string<. Grading runs against a pristine copy of these files
plus your answer.txt, so editing the harness changes nothing.

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(handler-case (progn (load "harness.lisp"))
  (error (c) (fail (format nil "the harness does not load: ~a" c))))

;; Ground truth is DERIVED, at grade time, by the real constructor -- the
;; family's whole lesson applied to its own grader.
(defvar *names*
  (handler-case (sort (copy-list (tool-names (sub-agent (make-workspace-agent :extras (list audit-tool))))) #'string<)
    (error (c) (fail (format nil "the constructor itself failed: ~a" c)))))

(unless (probe-file "answer.txt") (fail "no answer.txt"))
(let ((lines (with-open-file (in "answer.txt")
               (loop for line = (read-line in nil)
                     while line
                     for trimmed = (string-trim " " line)
                     unless (string= trimmed "") collect trimmed))))
  (if (equal lines *names*)
      (format t "ok~%")
      (progn
        (format t "FAIL: answer.txt does not match~%--- expected ---~%~{~a~%~}--- got ---~%~{~a~%~}"
                *names* lines)
        (sb-ext:exit :code 1))))

Let me trace through this.

The harness:
- `*base*` starts `'()`.
- `register` adds tool to `*base*`, removing any with same name.
- Registers "read", "edit", "grep" — so `*base*` = (grep edit read) in some order, since cons adds to front. After register "read": *base* = (read). After "edit": (edit read). After "grep": (grep edit read).
- `audit-tool` is a tool named "audit" but NOT registered.
- `make-workspace-agent` with `:extras (list audit-tool)` → `:tools (append *base* extras)` = (grep edit read audit).
- `sub-agent` ignores parent and returns `(list :tools *base* :extras '())` — so tools = *base* = (grep edit read).

So `tool-names` of the sub-agent = ("grep" "edit" "read"), sorted ascending by string< → "edit", "grep", "read".

The check.lisp derives ground truth at grade time by running the real constructor, so the answer is just what the constructor produces. Since registration is conditional (no condition here), names can be overridden (register removes duplicates), definition is not registration (audit-tool defined but never registered, so not in *base*).

So answer.txt should be:
edit
grep
read

Let me verify by running it. I'll write a probe.

Confirmed: the sub-agent receives tools from `*base*` only — "edit", "grep", "read". The audit-tool is defined but never registered, and sub-agent rebuilds from `*base*`, ignoring extras.

The probe confirms it: `sub-agent` rebuilds its tools from `*base*` (the registered tools "read", "edit", "grep"), ignoring the parent's `:extras`. The `audit-tool` is defined but never registered, so it never makes it in. Sorted ascending by `string<`: edit, grep, read.

Why: `sub-agent` ignores its parent entirely and rebuilds from the global registry `*base*`. Only `read`, `edit`, and `grep` were ever `register`ed; `audit-tool` is defined (`make-tool :name "audit"`) but never registered, so it is not part of `*base*` and never reaches the sub-agent. The probe run confirmed the constructor returns `edit`, `grep`, `read` sorted ascending by `string<`, matching the grader's derived ground truth (`ok`).
